facts.label: Document relationships and conflicts
facts.text: - Overlap, not independent corroboration. The fiscal Q3 release repeats the 10-Q statements. For example fiscal Q3 revenue is 1,278,971 thousand in both (10-Q_2026-06-30… page:4; EX-99.1_2026-08-06… page:6) and the balance sheets agree line by line. Treat the 10-Q as controlling and do not count the release as independent evidence. - Two EBITDA measures. The release's adjusted EBITDA for the quarter is $192,327 thousand (EX-99.1_2026-08-06… page:9) and the Credit Agreement's Consolidated EBITDA for the same quarter is $210,398 thousand (10-Q_2026-06-30… page:33). The definitions differ ("The definition of Consolidated EBITDA requires us to include adjustments not typically included within EBITDA", page:32). Downstream modules must keep the two measures apart and label which is used. The difference is accounted for by items printed in the two reconciliations (see Calculations); no figure is reconciled here. - Net leverage text. The release says the ratio was "2.0x" at June 30, 2026 and "1.8x at March 31, 2026" (EX-99.1_2026-08-06… page:4), while the 10-Qs print 2.00 and 1.75 for those dates (10-Q_2026-06-30… page:33; 10-Q_2026-03-31… page:30). They agree after rounding. The ratio uses the Credit Agreement definition, not a rebuilt one. - Liquidity text. The 10-K says "access to an additional $750.0 million through a revolving credit facility" at September 30, 2025 (page:52). The fiscal Q3 10-Q says "access to approximately $730.0 million" at June 30, 2026 while the debt table shows a $20,000 thousand revolver balance (10-Q_2026-06-30… pages:32, 15). The 10-K also states letters of credit of $3.0 million issued under the Credit Agreement at September 30, 2025 (page:84). No 10-Q mentions letters of credit (a search of the three 10-Qs for "letter" found nothing), so availability net of letters of credit at June 30, 2026 is not determinable. The 10-K also notes revolving credit facilities in Canada and the United Kingdom (page:83), with no size or balance, and the 10-Qs do not mention them. - Receivable-sale capacity. The maximum amount of receivables that may be sold at one time is $250.0 million in the 10-K and the fiscal Q1 10-Q (10-K… page:94; 10-Q_2025-12-31… page:17) and $350.0 million in the fiscal Q2 and Q3 10-Qs (10-Q_2026-03-31… page:18; 10-Q_2026-06-30… page:20). The change falls between December 31, 2025 and March 31, 2026; the sources give no date or terms for the increase. This is a change over time, not a conflict. - Guidance direction. Adjusted diluted EPS guidance was $8.25 to $8.55 in May 2026 (EX-99.1_2026-05-07… page:4) and is $7.90 to $8.20 in August 2026 (EX-99.1_2026-08-06… page:2). Free cash flow guidance was $450 million to $500 million in May (page:4 of that release) and is $425 million to $475 million in August (EX-99.1_2026-08-06… page:2). Both moved down. - Terminology: the 10-Qs call the whole agreement the "Credit Agreement" with a Term Loan A, a Term Loan B and a Revolver. Consumers should keep them as separate instruments.

facts.label: Analytical read-through
facts.text: - Usable coverage: the audited fiscal 2025 statements, three interim 10-Qs and three releases support a reported-basis financial foundation for fiscal Q3 2026, nine months 2026 and fiscal 2025, and a trailing twelve month view to June 30, 2026 built from fiscal 2025 plus nine months 2026 less nine months 2025, with all three components located (10-K… page:64; 10-Q_2026-06-30… page:4). The Credit Agreement's own trailing twelve month Consolidated EBITDA is also printed for each quarter (page:33). - Strongest contrary evidence: the covenant package is described only through the issuer's own disclosure. The 10-Q gives "Consolidated Net Total Leverage Ratio ... cannot exceed 4.00:1.00 ... with a step up to 4.50:1.00 under certain circumstances" and "cannot be less than 3.00:1.00" for coverage (page:32), and prints ratios of 2.00 and 8.72 (page:33). The definition of Consolidated EBITDA includes "estimated synergies from acquisitions" and "pro forma effects" (page:32), and the Credit Agreement text is not supplied. A downstream module that computes its own leverage from reported EBITDA will not match the printed ratio without the definition, and the source set cannot settle the difference. - Source-risk mechanism, cash flow. Operating cash flow was an outflow of $179.9 million for nine months ended June 30, 2026 and is described as affected by "administrative delays on payments from one of our large contracts with the U.S. federal government" (page:31). Receivables of $1.28 billion were sold to a bank in the nine months and recorded in operating cash flows (page:20). A reader who compares operating cash flow or days sales outstanding across periods without the receivable-sale effect would misread conversion: the 10-Q reports days sales outstanding of 98 days, or 123 days "Excluding the effects of the RPA" (page:31). The $245 million collected after June 30, 2026 is a subsequent event, and the fiscal fourth quarter that would show the effect is not supplied. - Perimeter risk: restricted cash of $96,296 thousand is held for customers within prepaid and other current assets, and the cash flow statement's ending balance of 153,249 thousand includes it while the balance sheet cash is 56,953 thousand (page:19, page:6). Liquidity work must use unrestricted cash. - What cannot proceed: legal ranking, collateral and guarantor coverage beyond the 10-K sentence; covenant testing on Credit Agreement definitions; amendment terms; any rating-based or market-price-based view, because no ratings, quotes or peers are supplied; fiscal 2026 full-year results; anything after August 6, 2026. - Next evidence action: supply the executed Credit Agreement with its May 27, 2026 amendment, the fiscal 2026 10-K and any fiscal Q4 release, the earnings presentations, any rating reports, and 8-K filings dated August 7, 2026 to the cutoff. Until then carry each limitation above into the modules.

For fiscal 2025 (10-K… page:54): 319,034 + 84,080 − 640 + 125,815 + 92,047 + 41,182 + 427 + 39,549 + 41,669 + 50,832 = 793,995, equal to the printed figure. - Printed ratios recomputed from printed inputs: (1,653,548 − 56,953) = 1,596,595; 1,596,595 / 798,419 = 2.00 (page:33). 798,419 / 91,588 = 8.72 (page:33). facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The reported financial base for MAXIMUS, INC. supports a moderately levered, covenant-compliant credit view at June 30, 2026, with the issuer-adjusted measures and the Credit Agreement measures kept apart. Revenue for the nine months ended June 30, 2026 was 3,929,984 thousand against 4,112,861 thousand a year earlier, operating income rose to 456,125 thousand from 405,427 thousand, and issuer-adjusted EBITDA was 550,768 thousand against 541,313 thousand; the operating income gain is largely explained by a 39,343 thousand divestiture charge in the prior-year figure, which the adjusted measure adds back. Net cash used in operating activities was 179,863 thousand against 220,000 thousand, which reflects the seasonal receivables build and, in the current year, delayed payments from a large federal contract, after 1.28 billion US dollars of receivables were sold to a bank. Total debt principal was 1,653,548 thousand against 1,346,875 thousand at September 30, 2025, and unrestricted cash fell to 56,953 thousand from 222,351 thousand, so net debt of 1,596,595 thousand is 2.25 times LTM issuer-adjusted EBITDA of 711,009 thousand (C5), up from 1.60 times. The issuer reports a Credit Agreement ratio of 2.00 against a 4.00 maximum, on its own EBITDA definition that adds 52,278 thousand of pro forma and other adjustments (C9). The stack is a single bank Credit Agreement: Term Loan A, Term Loan B and a 750,000 thousand revolver with 20,000 thousand drawn, secured by substantially all assets (10-K page:84); no bonds or indentures appear in the supplied sources. The nearest large maturity is 690,184 thousand in the year ending September 30, 2029. Open items are the Credit Agreement text and amendment terms, the receivable-sale balance outstanding, letters of credit, and the fiscal fourth quarter, which carries the collections that full-year free cash flow guidance requires (C13).

facts.label: Latest quarter and after
facts.text: - Fiscal Q3 2026 (three months ended June 30, 2026): revenue 1,278,971 thousand against 1,348,400 thousand, a decline of 5.1% (C7); adjusted EBITDA 192,327 against 198,289 (margin 15.0% against 14.7% as printed); operating income 161,428 against 165,672; net income 103,593 against 105,981 (Q3 10-Q page:4; Q3 release pages:2, 6, 9). All three segments reported lower revenue; the release attributes the prior-year quarter to "elevated natural disaster support activity as well as temporary clinical volume surges" (Q3 release page:3). - Financing event: on May 27, 2026 the Credit Agreement was amended and Term Loan B increased by 325 million US dollars (Q3 10-Q page:15). Term Loan B principal rose from 491,250 at March 31, 2026 to 814,173 at June 30, 2026 and the revolver fell from 225,000 to 20,000, so the quarter's borrowings of 703,675 and repayments of 600,935 are consistent with refinancing revolver borrowings (Q3 release page:7; C16). The amendment's pricing, maturity and other terms are Not supplied. Debt financing costs paid in the quarter were 2,393 thousand. New interest rate swaps took effect on June 1, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:16). - Capital returns: the board increased the repurchase authorization in May 2026 to up to 400 million US dollars, with about 400.0 million still available at June 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:19). In the nine months the company purchased about 2.6 million shares at a cost of 192.4 million including excise tax, against 204,919 thousand of cash purchases in the cash flow statement; the sources do not reconcile the two. Quarterly dividend 0.33 per share (Q3 10-Q page:5). - Operations and cash: days sales outstanding were 98 days at June 30, 2026 against 62 days at September 30, 2025, or 123 days against 73 days excluding the receivable-sale effect, because of "administrative delays on payments from one of our large contracts with the U.S. federal government" (Q3 10-Q page:31). Accounts receivable, net rose from 898,095 to 1,382,014 thousand (C14). rows.label: Net debt to issuer-adjusted EBITDA rose from 1.60x to 2.25x in nine months, and the reported covenant ratio is 2.00 against a 4.00 maximum. Cash flow is seasonal and full-year guidance rests on fourth-quarter collections.
Debt principal rose by 306,673 thousand US dollars between September 30, 2025 and June 30, 2026 while unrestricted cash fell to 56,953 thousand.
Nine-month operating cash flow was an outflow of 179,863 thousand and buybacks plus dividends took 256,356 thousand.
Liquidity at June 30, 2026 was 786,953 thousand: 56,953 of cash and about 730,000 of revolver capacity.
Reported covenant leverage is 2.00 against a 4.00 maximum, and interest cover is 8.72 against a 3.00 minimum.
August 2026 guidance lowered adjusted EPS, adjusted EBITDA margin and free cash flow after a customer-directed contract modification effective July 1, 2026.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: MAXIMUS, INC. is an independent, widely held provider of outsourced government services: program operations (eligibility, enrollment and contact centers), clinical assessments and technology services, delivered through three segments, U.S. Federal Services, U.S. Services and Outside the U.S. (10-K page:7 to page:11). There is no sponsor, no pending transaction and no acquisition of the issuer in the supplied sources, so the transaction row is Insufficient Information rather than an adverse finding. The creditor-relevant facts are business concentration and capital allocation. Revenue is anchored in government programs with a long backlog, but the 10-K states that approximately 60% of fiscal 2025 revenue came from the ten largest contracts and about one-fifth from a single federal agency (10-K page:19), and that "almost all" contracts permit termination for convenience (page:17). Cash conversion is lumpy because payments from government customers can be delayed: the fiscal Q3 10-Q reports days sales outstanding of 98 days against 62 days and links the delay to "one of our large contracts with the U.S. federal government" (Q3 10-Q page:31). Capital allocation has been shareholder-oriented: buybacks and a higher dividend were funded partly by expanding the term loans, and the CP-1 financial base shows net debt to issuer-adjusted EBITDA of 2.25x at June 30, 2026 against 1.60x at September 30, 2025, with the reported covenant ratio at 2.00 against a 4.00 maximum. A temporary contractual modification by a major customer, effective July 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026, cut fiscal 2026 earnings and free cash flow guidance in August 2026. The only financing event in the period is a May 27, 2026 amendment that added 325 million US dollars to Term Loan B. The open items for monitoring are the proxy statement (ownership and related parties), the Credit Agreement, the identity of the customers behind the largest contracts, and everything after August 6, 2026.

facts.label: Conflicts logged
facts.text: 1. Share purchase amount for fiscal 2025. The 10-K MD&A says "We have utilized $447.5 million in fiscal year 2025 to purchase 5.8 million shares of our common stock" (10-K page:51) and the cash flow statement shows "(447,482)" (10-K page:66), while the equity note says "we purchased 5.8 million and 0.9 million of our common shares at a cost of $456.6 million and $73.1 million" (10-K page:93). The 10-K does not state the basis of the 456.6 figure (the nine-month 2026 text similarly gives "$192.4 million, which includes an additional charge from the 1% excise tax" against 204,919 thousand of cash in the cash flow statement, Q3 10-Q page:19). Effect: any analysis of capital returned must name which figure it uses. 2. U.S. federal share of revenue. The segment text says "Our U.S. Federal Services Segment generated 56% of our total revenue in fiscal year 2025" (10-K page:7), the risk factor says "approximately 55% of our total revenue was derived from the U.S. federal government" (10-K page:18) and the customer table shows 55.2% (10-K page:80). These are different definitions (segment, customer type) and the 10-K does not state which segment contracts are non-federal or which federal revenue sits in other segments. Effect: concentration should be quoted with its definition. 3. Outside the U.S. margin outlook. The 10-K says "We anticipate operating margins for the Outside the U.S. Segment in fiscal year 2026 to range between 3% to 5%" (10-K page:49) and the fiscal Q3 10-Q says "For fiscal year 2026, we anticipate a breakeven operating margin" (Q3 10-Q page:29). This is a change in management's outlook between filings, not a restatement. Effect: the segment's contribution to fiscal 2026 earnings is lower than the annual report implied.

rows.label: Maximus is a widely held government services contractor with no sponsor and a heavy U.S. federal concentration. Management has raised leverage through partly debt-funded buybacks while a major customer modification lowers earnings through December 31, 2026.
About 55% of fiscal 2025 revenue came from the U.S. federal government, about 60% from the ten largest contracts and about one-fifth from a single federal agency.
No sponsor or controlling holder is disclosed; the 10-K reports 30 holders of record and about 151,000 beneficial owners.
Share purchases of 447,482 thousand in fiscal 2025 and 204,919 thousand in nine months 2026 were partly funded by credit facility expansions, and the dividend rose from 0.30 to 0.33.
Backlog was 15,327 million US dollars at September 30, 2025, down from 16,167 million, and the Outside the U.S. segment is guided to break even for fiscal 2026.
On May 27, 2026 Term Loan B was increased by 325 million; no sponsor deal, bond issue or acquisition of the issuer is described.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: MAXIMUS, INC. is a moderately levered, covenant-compliant government services credit whose weak point is seasonal, customer-driven cash flow rather than balance sheet leverage. Its strongest support is a USD 15,327 million backlog at September 30, 2025, a reported covenant leverage ratio of 2.00 against a 4.00 maximum, and bank debt that matures between fiscal 2029 and 2031. The weakest point is that net debt to issuer-adjusted EBITDA rose to 2.25x from 1.60x in nine months, nine-month free cash flow was an outflow of USD 208.6 million, cash is USD 57.0 million, and about 60% of revenue comes from ten contracts. What decides the outcome is whether the fourth-quarter collections that guidance requires arrive, and whether management keeps funding buybacks with debt while a major customer's modification runs to December 31, 2026.

Its strongest support is a USD 15,327 million backlog at September 30, 2025, a reported covenant leverage ratio of 2.00 against a 4.00 maximum, and bank debt that matures between fiscal 2029 and 2031. The weakest point is that net debt to issuer-adjusted EBITDA rose to 2.25x from 1.60x in nine months, nine-month free cash flow was an outflow of USD 208.6 million, cash is USD 57.0 million, and about 60% of revenue comes from ten contracts. What decides the outcome is whether the fourth-quarter collections that guidance requires arrive, and whether management keeps funding buybacks with debt while a major customer's modification runs to December 31, 2026.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 1. Leverage is moderate but rising. Total debt principal is USD 1,653.5 million and unrestricted cash USD 57.0 million, so net debt is USD 1,596.6 million, or 2.25x LTM issuer-adjusted EBITDA of USD 711.0 million (2.33x gross), against 1.60x at September 30, 2025. Debt principal rose USD 306.7 million and net debt USD 472.1 million in nine months [CP-1 C5, C11]. 2. Covenant headroom is wide on the reported definition. Consolidated net total leverage is 2.00 against a 4.00 maximum, so Credit Agreement EBITDA of USD 798.4 million could fall 50.0% before the test binds, and net interest coverage is 8.72 against a 3.00 minimum, a 65.6% cushion. The Credit Agreement EBITDA exceeds the issuer-adjusted measure by USD 87.4 million of stock compensation and pro forma adjustments, and the agreement and its definitions are not supplied, so the headroom is the issuer's own figure [CP-1 C9; CP-0 gaps]. 3. Cash flow is seasonal and delayed. Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 179.9 million in nine months and USD 469.5 million for the LTM, 66.0% of issuer-adjusted EBITDA. Days sales outstanding were 98 days against 62 because a large federal contract paid late; USD 245 million was collected after June 30, 2026. Full-year guidance implies fourth-quarter free cash flow of USD 633.6 million to USD 683.6 million, against USD 641.8 million delivered in the prior year's fourth quarter [CP-1 C3, C13; CP-1A]. 4. Shareholder returns are debt-funded. Nine-month buybacks of USD 204.9 million and dividends of USD 51.4 million, USD 256.4 million together, were met from net borrowing of USD 302.7 million and a USD 165.4 million fall in unrestricted cash, with other cash flows not itemised. Fiscal 2025 buybacks of USD 447.5 million were 6.5 times dividends. Management states a target leverage of 2x to 3x on the covenant definition, so the reported 2.00 sits at the bottom of the range [CP-1 C11; CP-1A governance]. 5. Liquidity is adequate but thin in cash. Liquidity is USD 787.0 million: cash USD 57.0 million plus USD 730.0 million of revolver capacity as printed, with letters of credit not stated and the USD 350.0 million receivable-sale facility excluded. Scheduled principal payments are USD 19.0 million for July to September 2026 and USD 75.8 million in fiscal 2027, covered 8.3 times by liquidity; the largest single-year bucket is USD 690.2 million in fiscal 2029 [CP-1 C10, maturities chart]. 6. Interest cost is exposed to floating rates. Swaps cover USD 675.0 million, 40.8% of principal; USD 978.5 million pays SOFR plus margin, so 100 basis points adds about USD 9.8 million a year. A USD 75.0 million Term Loan B swap expires in September 2026. The effective rate is 5.6% [CP-1 C12; C1 below]. 7. Earnings are down and the outlook was lowered. Nine-month revenue was USD 3,930.0 million, 4.4% lower, and fiscal Q3 revenue fell 5.1%, but issuer-adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 14.0% from 13.2%. In August 2026 adjusted EPS guidance fell to USD 7.90 to USD 8.20 from USD 8.25 to USD 8.55 and free cash flow guidance to USD 425 million to USD 475 million from USD 450 million to USD 500 million, after a customer modification effective July 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026 that management expects to reduce diluted EPS by about USD 0.35 per quarter [CP-1 latest quarter; CP-1A timeline]. 8. Revenue is concentrated and terminable. About 55% of fiscal 2025 revenue came from the U.S. federal government, about 60% from the ten largest contracts and about one-fifth from a single federal agency; almost all contracts permit termination for convenience. Backlog of USD 15,327 million is 2.82 times fiscal 2025 revenue but fell 5.2% in the year to September 30, 2025, and no later backlog is supplied [CP-1A operating model, C1, C2]. 9. Claims outside debt are modest but unquantified in places. Operating lease liabilities are USD 94.9 million; receivables of USD 1.28 billion were sold to a bank in nine months with the outstanding balance not printed; performance bonds were USD 33.2 million at September 30, 2025; the MOVEit litigation accrual is not stated; no defined benefit pension is described. Goodwill and intangibles exceed equity by USD 517.0 million [CP-1 claims table, C14]. 10. Governance is open on the facts that matter to creditors. There is no sponsor and no controlling holder disclosed (30 holders of record, about 151,000 beneficial owners), but the proxy statement, Credit Agreement, guarantors and change-of-control terms are not supplied, and three source conflicts are logged: the fiscal 2025 buyback amount, the federal revenue share definition and the Outside the U.S. margin outlook [CP-1A governance and conflicts].

facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: - C1, interest sensitivity (inference). Unhedged principal 419,375 + 539,173 + 20,000 = 978,548 thousand (CP-1 C12); a 100 basis point rise adds 978,548 x 1% = 9,785 thousand, USD 9.8 million a year, which is 11.3% of LTM cash interest paid of 86,279 thousand (9,785 / 86,279). It assumes a full year at the June 30, 2026 balances and ignores the September 2026 swap expiry. - C2, liquidity cover of near-term principal. Liquidity 786,953 thousand (CP-1 C10) / principal due July 2026 to September 2027, 18,952 + 75,809 = 94,761 thousand = 8.3x. Through fiscal 2028: 94,761 + 81,434 = 176,195 thousand, 4.5x. - C3, room to the top of management's range (Credit Agreement basis, illustrative). At 3.00x on Credit Agreement EBITDA of 798,419 thousand, net debt would be 2,395,257 thousand against 1,596,595 thousand today, an increase of 798,662 thousand. At the 4.00 covenant maximum the increase is 1,597,081 thousand (CP-1 C9). This ignores EBITDA change and is not a forecast or a capacity statement. - C4, shareholder returns against cash generation. LTM dividends 68,282 + LTM share purchases 345,958 = 414,240 thousand, 95.6% of LTM free cash flow of 433,230 thousand (CP-1 C1, C3). Nine months: returns 256,356 thousand against free cash flow of −208,615 thousand, a gap of 464,971 thousand; net borrowing of 302,740 and a fall in unrestricted cash of 222,351 − 56,953 = 165,398 together are 468,138 thousand, and other cash flows are not itemised here. - C5, capitalization. Debt principal 1,653,548 / (1,653,548 + equity 1,740,551) = 48.7%. Goodwill plus intangibles of 2,257,574 exceed equity by 517,023 (CP-1 C14). - C6, leverage including operating leases (illustrative). Principal 1,653,548 + operating lease liabilities 94,883 = 1,748,431 thousand; / LTM issuer-adjusted EBITDA 711,009 = 2.46x. Net of unrestricted cash: (1,748,431 − 56,953) = 1,691,478 / 711,009 = 2.38x. Lease expense is inside EBITDA, so this overstates leverage and is shown only as a sensitivity. - C7, collections already received against guidance. Implied fourth-quarter free cash flow 633,615 to 683,615 thousand (CP-1 C13); the 245,000 thousand collected after June 30, 2026 is 38.7% to 35.8% of it (245,000 / 633,615 and 245,000 / 683,615). The 245,000 is operating cash received and not net of fourth-quarter outflows. - C8, upstream figures reused. Leverage, cover, covenant headroom, liquidity, maturities, hedge share, backlog ratios and revenue shares are taken from CP-1 (C1 to C16) and CP-1A (C1 to C8) and are not recomputed.

- **C3, room to the top of management's range (Credit Agreement basis, illustrative).** At 3.00x on Credit Agreement EBITDA of 798,419 thousand, net debt would be 2,395,257 thousand against 1,596,595 thousand today, an increase of 798,662 thousand. At the 4.00 covenant maximum the increase is 1,597,081 thousand (CP-1 C9). This ignores EBITDA change and is not a forecast or a capacity statement.

- **C4, shareholder returns against cash generation.** LTM dividends 68,282 + LTM share purchases 345,958 = 414,240 thousand, 95.6% of LTM free cash flow of 433,230 thousand (CP-1 C1, C3). Nine months: returns 256,356 thousand against free cash flow of −208,615 thousand, a gap of 464,971 thousand; net borrowing of 302,740 and a fall in unrestricted cash of 222,351 − 56,953 = 165,398 together are 468,138 thousand, and other cash flows are not itemised here.
- **C5, capitalization.** Debt principal 1,653,548 / (1,653,548 + equity 1,740,551) = 48.7%. Goodwill plus intangibles of 2,257,574 exceed equity by 517,023 (CP-1 C14).

- **C6, leverage including operating leases (illustrative).** Principal 1,653,548 + operating lease liabilities 94,883 = 1,748,431 thousand; / LTM issuer-adjusted EBITDA 711,009 = 2.46x. Net of unrestricted cash: (1,748,431 − 56,953) = 1,691,478 / 711,009 = 2.38x. Lease expense is inside EBITDA, so this overstates leverage and is shown only as a sensitivity.

- **C7, collections already received against guidance.** Implied fourth-quarter free cash flow 633,615 to 683,615 thousand (CP-1 C13); the 245,000 thousand collected after June 30, 2026 is 38.7% to 35.8% of it (245,000 / 633,615 and 245,000 / 683,615). The 245,000 is operating cash received and not net of fourth-quarter outflows.

- **C8, upstream figures reused.** Leverage, cover, covenant headroom, liquidity, maturities, hedge share, backlog ratios and revenue shares are taken from CP-1 (C1 to C16) and CP-1A (C1 to C8) and are not recomputed.

rows.label: Maximus is a moderately levered, covenant-compliant government services credit. Net leverage has risen to 2.25x on buybacks and a receivables build, and liquidity depends on fourth-quarter collections and the revolver.
Net debt to issuer-adjusted EBITDA is 2.25x against 1.60x nine months earlier, and the reported covenant ratio is 2.00 against a 4.00 maximum.
Nine-month free cash flow was an outflow of USD 208.6 million, and the issuer needs fourth-quarter free cash flow of USD 633.6 million to USD 683.6 million to meet guidance.
Liquidity is USD 787.0 million, of which USD 57.0 million is cash and USD 730.0 million is revolver capacity.
About 60% of revenue comes from the ten largest contracts and about 55% from the U.S. federal government.
Buybacks exceeded dividends 6.5 times in fiscal 2025 and were partly debt-funded.

Fundamental credit view: moderately levered, covenant-compliant government services operator with long contract visibility, rising leverage, seasonal cash flow and heavy contract concentration; the fourth-quarter collections and the capital allocation policy are the main watch items
Business risk: moderate, supported by backlog and essential government programs, offset by contract concentration, termination rights and a lowered outlook
Financial risk: moderate on 2.25x net leverage and wide reported covenant headroom, with cash flow timing risk
Collection timing on a large federal contract

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The seven filed documents and releases are enough to start all four requested downstream modules on the consolidated company, with limitations. Filed statements control; releases are attributed support. | Medium | Credit agreement text, ratings, fiscal fourth quarter results and earnings presentations are not supplied, so legal terms cannot be verified and nothing after August 6, 2026 is covered. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Audited fiscal 2025 statements, three quarterly reports and three releases give a continuous record from September 30, 2025 to June 30, 2026. | Debt, liquidity and cash flow work can proceed on filed figures for the quarter, nine months and fiscal 2025. | High |

| Both financial covenants, their levels, the reported ratios and the covenant EBITDA reconciliation are printed, but the Credit Agreement itself is not supplied. | Headroom can be quoted from the filings; definitions, baskets and amendment terms cannot be verified. | Medium |
| A May 27, 2026 amendment added $325 million to Term Loan B; the filing prints no other amendment terms. | The post-amendment maturity wall and pricing rest on the note tables alone. | Medium |

| Receivable sales under a bank agreement sit inside operating cash flow, and payments from a large federal customer were delayed. | Cash conversion and liquidity need a label for the receivable-sale effect and the timing of collections. | Medium |
| No ratings, earnings presentations, guarantor names or fiscal 2026 annual results are supplied. | Instrument ranking, rating view and full-year fiscal 2026 results stay as gaps. | Medium |
### Readiness view

The effective source set can support the minimum module set for MAXIMUS, INC. with limitations. All seven issuer sources are filed SEC documents or furnished earnings releases of one registrant, with text extracted from the original HTML. The audited fiscal 2025 statements, three unaudited 2026 interim filings and three releases give a continuous record from September 30, 2025 to June 30, 2026, and the latest document is dated August 6, 2026. Nothing is blocked on identity. Each of the four consumers is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS. None is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED. This is source sufficiency only; it does not say that downstream analysis is complete or that any model input contract is met.
### Information-availability boundary

- Every supplied document is dated on or before August 6, 2026, before the cutoff of 2026-11-05. The latest are the fiscal Q3 2026 10-Q, signed "/s/ Bruce L. Caswell August 6, 2026" (`10-Q_2026-06-30…` page:39), and the fiscal Q3 release, "Date: August 6, 2026" (`EX-99.1_2026-08-06…` page:1).

- Nothing dated between August 7, 2026 and the cutoff is supplied. That window contains the end of the fiscal year (September 30, 2026). The fiscal 2026 annual report, any fiscal fourth quarter release, and any 8-K, financing event or rating action in the window are Not supplied, not absent. The host infers, without evidence from the pack, that the fiscal 2026 10-K may fall after the cutoff because the fiscal 2025 10-K was signed on November 20, 2025 (`10-K_2025-09-30…` page:105). That inference does not establish whether any later document exists before the cutoff.

- Post-balance-sheet events in the fiscal Q3 10-Q: a quarterly dividend of $0.33 per share declared July 6, 2026, payable August 31, 2026, about $17.3 million (page:22); and "Subsequent to June 30, 2026, we have received $245 million of cash due from this customer" (page:31). The temporary contractual modification on a major federal program runs "effective July 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026" (page:27), so part of its effect falls after the balance sheet date.
- The fiscal 2025 10-K reports its own subsequent event: a dividend of $0.30 per share declared October 6, 2025 (`10-K_2025-09-30…` page:99).
### Identity and perimeter

- Reporting entity: Maximus, Inc., a Virginia corporation, "Commission file number: 1-12997", common stock listed on the New York Stock Exchange as MMS, large accelerated filer (`10-K_2025-09-30…` page:1; `10-Q_2026-06-30…` page:1). All statements are consolidated. No parent is named in the supplied text; the context parent is blank.

- Debt perimeter. The 10-K states: "The Credit Agreement is, subject to customary exceptions, secured by substantially all of our assets and all of the assets of our wholly owned material domestic subsidiaries, and guaranteed by each of our wholly owned material domestic subsidiaries" (`10-K_2025-09-30…` page:84). The guarantor entities are not named, the borrower entity is not separated from the registrant, and the restricted or unrestricted split is not stated in any supplied source. The 10-Qs do not repeat the security and guarantee sentence (a search of all three 10-Qs and the three releases for "secured by", "guaranteed by" and "guarantor" found nothing). The context guarantor list is blank. This is an unresolved perimeter gap.

- Units and currency: statements are in thousands of USD ("(in thousands, except per share amounts)", `10-Q_2026-06-30…` page:4). MD&A text and the releases mix millions, billions and thousands. Operations also run in the United Kingdom, Canada and the Middle East, and a foreign currency translation line appears in comprehensive income (page:5); statements are nonetheless presented in USD, which matches the context currency. No other reporting currency is used.

- Fiscal calendar: fiscal year ends September 30. Quarterly statements carry three-month and nine-month columns; the cash flow statement in the 10-Q is nine-month only, while the release adds a three-month cash flow column (`EX-99.1_2026-08-06…` page:7).

- Auditor: KPMG LLP, report dated "November 20, 2025", "We have served as the Company's auditor since 2024" (`10-K_2025-09-30…` page:63). The fiscal 2024 comparatives carry a separate Ernst & Young LLP report dated November 21, 2024 (page:64). Interim statements are unaudited.
### Source register
#### Form 10-K for fiscal 2025
- Family and authority: filed annual report, original authority for audited consolidated statements for the years ended September 30, 2025, 2024 and 2023. Signed November 20, 2025 (page:105).

- Located: statement of operations page:64, balance sheet pages:64 to 65, cash flows pages:65 to 66, business pages:4 to 17, risk factors pages:18 to 38, cybersecurity page:39, MD&A results page:44, backlog page:49, liquidity and cash requirements pages:50 to 54, non-GAAP measures pages:58 to 59, segment note page:78, revenue disaggregation page:80, debt note pages:83 to 84 (debt table, maturities and swaps), leases page:89, receivable-sale agreement page:94, litigation pages:96 to 97, subsequent event page:99.
- Period and basis: fiscal years ended September 30, 2025, 2024 and 2023. Page:64 heads the columns "2025 2024 2023".

- Limits: exhibits are listed by reference only (page:104); no exhibit text, including the Credit Agreement, is supplied. Part III is incorporated from a proxy statement that is not supplied (page:2).
#### Forms 10-Q for fiscal Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026
- Family and authority: filed quarterly reports with unaudited condensed consolidated statements.

- Fiscal Q3 (June 30, 2026): statement of operations page:4, comprehensive income page:5, balance sheet pages:5 to 6, cash flows page:6, segment note pages:10 to 12, revenue disaggregation page:12, divestitures page:15, debt note and maturities pages:15 to 16, swaps pages:16 to 17, fair value page:17, equity and repurchases page:19, cash and restricted cash page:19, receivable-sale agreement page:20, litigation pages:21 to 22, subsequent event page:22, results of operations pages:22 to 29, liquidity and credit facilities pages:29 to 33, free cash flow pages:33 to 34, non-GAAP pages:35 to 36, signatures page:39.
- Fiscal Q1 (December 31, 2025): debt note page:13, receivable-sale agreement page:17, covenant tables pages:28 to 29, subsequent event page:19.
- Fiscal Q2 (March 31, 2026): debt note page:14, receivable-sale agreement page:18, covenant tables pages:30 to 31, subsequent event page:20.

- Period and basis: Q1 is three months. Q2 and Q3 carry three-month and year-to-date columns for the income statement; the cash flow statements in the 10-Qs are year-to-date, so a discrete quarter needs the release or subtraction downstream. This module does not do it.
#### Earnings releases (Exhibit 99.1) for fiscal Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026

- Family and authority: issuer press releases furnished as Exhibit 99.1, unaudited and management-prepared. They give reported and adjusted figures, guidance, pipeline statistics and quarter narrative. They are attributed management claims; the 10-Q controls where the two overlap.

- Located in the fiscal Q3 release: highlights page:2, segment narrative, pipeline and leverage statement pages:3 to 4, guidance reconciliation pages:5 to 6, statements of operations page:6, balance sheet pages:6 to 7, cash flows pages:7 to 8, segment results pages:8 to 9, free cash flow and adjusted EBITDA reconciliation page:9. The Q1 release has its leverage statement on page:5 and the Q2 release on page:4.

- Non-GAAP: "adjusted EBITDA", "adjusted diluted earnings per share" and "free cash flow" are the issuer's measures. The releases say that calculation details "are included with our earnings presentation and forthcoming Form 10-Q" (`EX-99.1_2026-08-06…` page:5); no earnings presentation is supplied.
### Document relationships and conflicts

- Overlap, not independent corroboration. The fiscal Q3 release repeats the 10-Q statements. For example fiscal Q3 revenue is 1,278,971 thousand in both (`10-Q_2026-06-30…` page:4; `EX-99.1_2026-08-06…` page:6) and the balance sheets agree line by line. Treat the 10-Q as controlling and do not count the release as independent evidence.

- Two EBITDA measures. The release's adjusted EBITDA for the quarter is $192,327 thousand (`EX-99.1_2026-08-06…` page:9) and the Credit Agreement's Consolidated EBITDA for the same quarter is $210,398 thousand (`10-Q_2026-06-30…` page:33). The definitions differ ("The definition of Consolidated EBITDA requires us to include adjustments not typically included within EBITDA", page:32). Downstream modules must keep the two measures apart and label which is used. The difference is accounted for by items printed in the two reconciliations (see Calculations); no figure is reconciled here.

- Net leverage text. The release says the ratio was "2.0x" at June 30, 2026 and "1.8x at March 31, 2026" (`EX-99.1_2026-08-06…` page:4), while the 10-Qs print 2.00 and 1.75 for those dates (`10-Q_2026-06-30…` page:33; `10-Q_2026-03-31…` page:30). They agree after rounding. The ratio uses the Credit Agreement definition, not a rebuilt one.

- Liquidity text. The 10-K says "access to an additional $750.0 million through a revolving credit facility" at September 30, 2025 (page:52). The fiscal Q3 10-Q says "access to approximately $730.0 million" at June 30, 2026 while the debt table shows a $20,000 thousand revolver balance (`10-Q_2026-06-30…` pages:32, 15). The 10-K also states letters of credit of $3.0 million issued under the Credit Agreement at September 30, 2025 (page:84). No 10-Q mentions letters of credit (a search of the three 10-Qs for "letter" found nothing), so availability net of letters of credit at June 30, 2026 is not determinable. The 10-K also notes revolving credit facilities in Canada and the United Kingdom (page:83), with no size or balance, and the 10-Qs do not mention them.

- Receivable-sale capacity. The maximum amount of receivables that may be sold at one time is $250.0 million in the 10-K and the fiscal Q1 10-Q (`10-K…` page:94; `10-Q_2025-12-31…` page:17) and $350.0 million in the fiscal Q2 and Q3 10-Qs (`10-Q_2026-03-31…` page:18; `10-Q_2026-06-30…` page:20). The change falls between December 31, 2025 and March 31, 2026; the sources give no date or terms for the increase. This is a change over time, not a conflict.

- Guidance direction. Adjusted diluted EPS guidance was $8.25 to $8.55 in May 2026 (`EX-99.1_2026-05-07…` page:4) and is $7.90 to $8.20 in August 2026 (`EX-99.1_2026-08-06…` page:2). Free cash flow guidance was $450 million to $500 million in May (page:4 of that release) and is $425 million to $475 million in August (`EX-99.1_2026-08-06…` page:2). Both moved down.
- Terminology: the 10-Qs call the whole agreement the "Credit Agreement" with a Term Loan A, a Term Loan B and a Revolver. Consumers should keep them as separate instruments.
### Consumer evidence demand

| CP-1 | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Annual and interim statements, segments, debt, cash flow, non-GAAP | 10-K pages:64 to 66, 78 to 80, 83 to 84, 58 to 59; fiscal Q3 10-Q pages:4 to 6, 10 to 12, 15 to 17, 33 to 36; releases pages:6 to 9 of the fiscal Q3 release | Two EBITDA definitions; discrete quarter cash flows only in the releases; no trailing twelve month adjusted EBITDA printed; letters of credit and non-US facilities not quantified at June 30, 2026; text extraction flattens tables |

### Analytical read-through

- Usable coverage: the audited fiscal 2025 statements, three interim 10-Qs and three releases support a reported-basis financial foundation for fiscal Q3 2026, nine months 2026 and fiscal 2025, and a trailing twelve month view to June 30, 2026 built from fiscal 2025 plus nine months 2026 less nine months 2025, with all three components located (`10-K…` page:64; `10-Q_2026-06-30…` page:4). The Credit Agreement's own trailing twelve month Consolidated EBITDA is also printed for each quarter (page:33).

- Strongest contrary evidence: the covenant package is described only through the issuer's own disclosure. The 10-Q gives "Consolidated Net Total Leverage Ratio ... cannot exceed 4.00:1.00 ... with a step up to 4.50:1.00 under certain circumstances" and "cannot be less than 3.00:1.00" for coverage (page:32), and prints ratios of 2.00 and 8.72 (page:33). The definition of Consolidated EBITDA includes "estimated synergies from acquisitions" and "pro forma effects" (page:32), and the Credit Agreement text is not supplied. A downstream module that computes its own leverage from reported EBITDA will not match the printed ratio without the definition, and the source set cannot settle the difference.

- Source-risk mechanism, cash flow. Operating cash flow was an outflow of $179.9 million for nine months ended June 30, 2026 and is described as affected by "administrative delays on payments from one of our large contracts with the U.S. federal government" (page:31). Receivables of $1.28 billion were sold to a bank in the nine months and recorded in operating cash flows (page:20). A reader who compares operating cash flow or days sales outstanding across periods without the receivable-sale effect would misread conversion: the 10-Q reports days sales outstanding of 98 days, or 123 days "Excluding the effects of the RPA" (page:31). The $245 million collected after June 30, 2026 is a subsequent event, and the fiscal fourth quarter that would show the effect is not supplied.

- Perimeter risk: restricted cash of $96,296 thousand is held for customers within prepaid and other current assets, and the cash flow statement's ending balance of 153,249 thousand includes it while the balance sheet cash is 56,953 thousand (page:19, page:6). Liquidity work must use unrestricted cash.

- What cannot proceed: legal ranking, collateral and guarantor coverage beyond the 10-K sentence; covenant testing on Credit Agreement definitions; amendment terms; any rating-based or market-price-based view, because no ratings, quotes or peers are supplied; fiscal 2026 full-year results; anything after August 6, 2026.

- Next evidence action: supply the executed Credit Agreement with its May 27, 2026 amendment, the fiscal 2026 10-K and any fiscal Q4 release, the earnings presentations, any rating reports, and 8-K filings dated August 7, 2026 to the cutoff. Until then carry each limitation above into the modules.
## Calculations

No new calculation is made for readiness. The checks below are source tie-outs that support the document relationships recorded above. They are not normalized or reconciled figures. Amounts are in thousands of USD unless stated.

- Fiscal Q3 debt table foots (`10-Q_2026-06-30…` page:15): Term Loan A 819,375 + Term Loan B 814,173 + Revolver 20,000 = 1,653,548, which equals "Total debt principal". Less unamortized debt-issuance costs and discounts 16,613 = 1,636,935, which equals "Total debt".
- Fiscal Q3 maturity table foots (page:15): 18,952 + 75,809 + 81,434 + 690,184 + 8,309 + 778,860 = 1,653,548, equal to the principal total.
- Fiscal 2025 maturity table foots (`10-K…` page:84): 55,625 + 72,500 + 78,125 + 666,875 + 5,000 + 468,750 = 1,346,875, equal to "Total debt principal" at September 30, 2025 (page:83).

- Interest rate swap notional (`10-Q_2026-06-30…` page:16): 75,000 + 75,000 + 150,000 + 200,000 + 75,000 + 50,000 + 50,000 = 675,000, which equals the $450 million asset notional plus the $225 million liability notional in the fair value table (page:17).

- Credit Agreement EBITDA reconciliation for the trailing twelve months to June 30, 2026 (page:33): 370,887 + 89,237 − 1,676 + 120,539 + 83,791 + 35,132 + 6,914 − 9,941 + 51,258 + 52,278 = 798,419, equal to the printed Consolidated EBITDA. For fiscal 2025 (`10-K…` page:54): 319,034 + 84,080 − 640 + 125,815 + 92,047 + 41,182 + 427 + 39,549 + 41,669 + 50,832 = 793,995, equal to the printed figure.

- Difference between the two EBITDA measures for fiscal Q3 2026: 210,398 − 192,327 = 18,071. The Credit Agreement reconciliation shows stock compensation expense 7,356 and pro forma and other adjustments 10,715 (page:33), and 7,356 + 10,715 = 18,071. The release's adjusted EBITDA reconciliation (`EX-99.1_2026-08-06…` page:9) has no stock compensation or pro forma line. This is a tie-out of printed items, not a reconciliation of definitions.

- Revolver capacity arithmetic: 750,000 − 20,000 = 730,000, equal to the "approximately $730.0 million" access in the 10-Q (page:32). This leaves no deduction for letters of credit, which the 10-Qs do not mention.
- Cash tie: balance sheet cash 56,953 + restricted cash 96,296 = 153,249, equal to the cash flow statement ending balance (page:19, page:6). At September 30, 2025: 222,351 + 38,108 = 260,459.
- Days between the latest document and the cutoff: August 6, 2026 to November 5, 2026 is 91 days.

### Financial base view

The reported financial base for MAXIMUS, INC. supports a moderately levered, covenant-compliant credit view at June 30, 2026, with the issuer-adjusted measures and the Credit Agreement measures kept apart. Revenue for the nine months ended June 30, 2026 was 3,929,984 thousand against 4,112,861 thousand a year earlier, operating income rose to 456,125 thousand from 405,427 thousand, and issuer-adjusted EBITDA was 550,768 thousand against 541,313 thousand; the operating income gain is largely explained by a 39,343 thousand divestiture charge in the prior-year figure, which the adjusted measure adds back. Net cash used in operating activities was 179,863 thousand against 220,000 thousand, which reflects the seasonal receivables build and, in the current year, delayed payments from a large federal contract, after 1.28 billion US dollars of receivables were sold to a bank. Total debt principal was 1,653,548 thousand against 1,346,875 thousand at September 30, 2025, and unrestricted cash fell to 56,953 thousand from 222,351 thousand, so net debt of 1,596,595 thousand is 2.25 times LTM issuer-adjusted EBITDA of 711,009 thousand (C5), up from 1.60 times. The issuer reports a Credit Agreement ratio of 2.00 against a 4.00 maximum, on its own EBITDA definition that adds 52,278 thousand of pro forma and other adjustments (C9). The stack is a single bank Credit Agreement: Term Loan A, Term Loan B and a 750,000 thousand revolver with 20,000 thousand drawn, secured by substantially all assets (10-K page:84); no bonds or indentures appear in the supplied sources. The nearest large maturity is 690,184 thousand in the year ending September 30, 2029. Open items are the Credit Agreement text and amendment terms, the receivable-sale balance outstanding, letters of credit, and the fiscal fourth quarter, which carries the collections that full-year free cash flow guidance requires (C13).

### Business and transaction view

MAXIMUS, INC. is an independent, widely held provider of outsourced government services: program operations (eligibility, enrollment and contact centers), clinical assessments and technology services, delivered through three segments, U.S. Federal Services, U.S. Services and Outside the U.S. (10-K page:7 to page:11). There is no sponsor, no pending transaction and no acquisition of the issuer in the supplied sources, so the transaction row is Insufficient Information rather than an adverse finding. The creditor-relevant facts are business concentration and capital allocation. Revenue is anchored in government programs with a long backlog, but the 10-K states that approximately 60% of fiscal 2025 revenue came from the ten largest contracts and about one-fifth from a single federal agency (10-K page:19), and that "almost all" contracts permit termination for convenience (page:17). Cash conversion is lumpy because payments from government customers can be delayed: the fiscal Q3 10-Q reports days sales outstanding of 98 days against 62 days and links the delay to "one of our large contracts with the U.S. federal government" (Q3 10-Q page:31). Capital allocation has been shareholder-oriented: buybacks and a higher dividend were funded partly by expanding the term loans, and the CP-1 financial base shows net debt to issuer-adjusted EBITDA of 2.25x at June 30, 2026 against 1.60x at September 30, 2025, with the reported covenant ratio at 2.00 against a 4.00 maximum. A temporary contractual modification by a major customer, effective July 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026, cut fiscal 2026 earnings and free cash flow guidance in August 2026. The only financing event in the period is a May 27, 2026 amendment that added 325 million US dollars to Term Loan B. The open items for monitoring are the proxy statement (ownership and related parties), the Credit Agreement, the identity of the customers behind the largest contracts, and everything after August 6, 2026.

Conflicts are logged, not reconciled.

1. Share purchase amount for fiscal 2025. The 10-K prints 56%, 32% and 11%. State and local agencies: 1,764,683 / 5,431,276 = 32.5% (10-K page:80).

- C7. Clinical services share change: 38.7% in fiscal 2025 against 30.3% in fiscal 2023, a rise of 8.4 percentage points (10-K page:80).

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Maximus is a moderately levered, covenant-compliant government services credit. Net leverage has risen to 2.25x on buybacks and a receivables build, and liquidity depends on fourth-quarter collections and the revolver. | Medium | The Credit Agreement, ratings, ownership detail and everything after August 6, 2026 are not supplied, so creditor protections and fiscal 2026 outcomes cannot be verified. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Net debt to issuer-adjusted EBITDA is 2.25x against 1.60x nine months earlier, and the reported covenant ratio is 2.00 against a 4.00 maximum. | Leverage is moderate and covenant headroom is wide, but the trend is upward and management's range allows more. | High |

| Nine-month free cash flow was an outflow of USD 208.6 million, and the issuer needs fourth-quarter free cash flow of USD 633.6 million to USD 683.6 million to meet guidance. | Debt service relies on a large, customer-dependent collection in one quarter. | Medium |

| Liquidity is USD 787.0 million, of which USD 57.0 million is cash and USD 730.0 million is revolver capacity. | The revolver is the buffer; letters of credit are not netted and the nearest large maturity is in fiscal 2029. | Medium |

| About 60% of revenue comes from the ten largest contracts and about 55% from the U.S. federal government. | One contract decision changes earnings and cash quickly, as the customer modification through December 31, 2026 shows. | High |

| Buybacks exceeded dividends 6.5 times in fiscal 2025 and were partly debt-funded. | Willingness to relever is documented, and the Credit Agreement limits on distributions are not supplied. | Medium |
### Credit view

MAXIMUS, INC. is a moderately levered, covenant-compliant government services credit whose weak point is seasonal, customer-driven cash flow rather than balance sheet leverage. Its strongest support is a USD 15,327 million backlog at September 30, 2025, a reported covenant leverage ratio of 2.00 against a 4.00 maximum, and bank debt that matures between fiscal 2029 and 2031. The weakest point is that net debt to issuer-adjusted EBITDA rose to 2.25x from 1.60x in nine months, nine-month free cash flow was an outflow of USD 208.6 million, cash is USD 57.0 million, and about 60% of revenue comes from ten contracts. What decides the outcome is whether the fourth-quarter collections that guidance requires arrive, and whether management keeps funding buybacks with debt while a major customer's modification runs to December 31, 2026.
### Key findings

1. Leverage is moderate but rising. Total debt principal is USD 1,653.5 million and unrestricted cash USD 57.0 million, so net debt is USD 1,596.6 million, or 2.25x LTM issuer-adjusted EBITDA of USD 711.0 million (2.33x gross), against 1.60x at September 30, 2025. Debt principal rose USD 306.7 million and net debt USD 472.1 million in nine months [CP-1 C5, C11].

2. Covenant headroom is wide on the reported definition. Consolidated net total leverage is 2.00 against a 4.00 maximum, so Credit Agreement EBITDA of USD 798.4 million could fall 50.0% before the test binds, and net interest coverage is 8.72 against a 3.00 minimum, a 65.6% cushion. The Credit Agreement EBITDA exceeds the issuer-adjusted measure by USD 87.4 million of stock compensation and pro forma adjustments, and the agreement and its definitions are not supplied, so the headroom is the issuer's own figure [CP-1 C9; CP-0 gaps].

3. Cash flow is seasonal and delayed. Operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 179.9 million in nine months and USD 469.5 million for the LTM, 66.0% of issuer-adjusted EBITDA. Days sales outstanding were 98 days against 62 because a large federal contract paid late; USD 245 million was collected after June 30, 2026. Full-year guidance implies fourth-quarter free cash flow of USD 633.6 million to USD 683.6 million, against USD 641.8 million delivered in the prior year's fourth quarter [CP-1 C3, C13; CP-1A].

4. Shareholder returns are debt-funded. Nine-month buybacks of USD 204.9 million and dividends of USD 51.4 million, USD 256.4 million together, were met from net borrowing of USD 302.7 million and a USD 165.4 million fall in unrestricted cash, with other cash flows not itemised. Fiscal 2025 buybacks of USD 447.5 million were 6.5 times dividends. Management states a target leverage of 2x to 3x on the covenant definition, so the reported 2.00 sits at the bottom of the range [CP-1 C11; CP-1A governance].

5. Liquidity is adequate but thin in cash. Liquidity is USD 787.0 million: cash USD 57.0 million plus USD 730.0 million of revolver capacity as printed, with letters of credit not stated and the USD 350.0 million receivable-sale facility excluded. Scheduled principal payments are USD 19.0 million for July to September 2026 and USD 75.8 million in fiscal 2027, covered 8.3 times by liquidity; the largest single-year bucket is USD 690.2 million in fiscal 2029 [CP-1 C10, maturities chart].

6. Interest cost is exposed to floating rates. Swaps cover USD 675.0 million, 40.8% of principal; USD 978.5 million pays SOFR plus margin, so 100 basis points adds about USD 9.8 million a year. A USD 75.0 million Term Loan B swap expires in September 2026. The effective rate is 5.6% [CP-1 C12; C1 below].

7. Earnings are down and the outlook was lowered. Nine-month revenue was USD 3,930.0 million, 4.4% lower, and fiscal Q3 revenue fell 5.1%, but issuer-adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 14.0% from 13.2%. In August 2026 adjusted EPS guidance fell to USD 7.90 to USD 8.20 from USD 8.25 to USD 8.55 and free cash flow guidance to USD 425 million to USD 475 million from USD 450 million to USD 500 million, after a customer modification effective July 1, 2026 through December 31, 2026 that management expects to reduce diluted EPS by about USD 0.35 per quarter [CP-1 latest quarter; CP-1A timeline].

8. Revenue is concentrated and terminable. About 55% of fiscal 2025 revenue came from the U.S. federal government, about 60% from the ten largest contracts and about one-fifth from a single federal agency; almost all contracts permit termination for convenience. Backlog of USD 15,327 million is 2.82 times fiscal 2025 revenue but fell 5.2% in the year to September 30, 2025, and no later backlog is supplied [CP-1A operating model, C1, C2].

9. Claims outside debt are modest but unquantified in places. Operating lease liabilities are USD 94.9 million; receivables of USD 1.28 billion were sold to a bank in nine months with the outstanding balance not printed; performance bonds were USD 33.2 million at September 30, 2025; the MOVEit litigation accrual is not stated; no defined benefit pension is described. Goodwill and intangibles exceed equity by USD 517.0 million [CP-1 claims table, C14].

10. Governance is open on the facts that matter to creditors. There is no sponsor and no controlling holder disclosed (30 holders of record, about 151,000 beneficial owners), but the proxy statement, Credit Agreement, guarantors and change-of-control terms are not supplied, and three source conflicts are logged: the fiscal 2025 buyback amount, the federal revenue share definition and the Outside the U.S. margin outlook [CP-1A governance and conflicts].
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Backlog and contract tenure: USD 15,327 million of backlog with about 5.0 years of average remaining life, including options, gives multi-year visibility [Documentary Fact; CP-1A operating model]. Simple, bank-only capital structure: one Credit Agreement with Term Loan A, Term Loan B and a USD 750 million revolver, with no bonds and scheduled principal payments below USD 100 million in each period before fiscal 2029 [Documentary Fact; CP-1 debt register]. Covenant headroom as reported: 2.00 against 4.00 and 8.72 against 3.00 [Documentary Fact, issuer-reported; CP-1]. Cash conversion over a full cycle: fiscal 2025 free cash flow of USD 366.2 million and LTM free cash flow of USD 433.2 million, which includes the prior year's strong fourth quarter [Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1 C3]. Margin improvement: issuer-adjusted EBITDA margin of 14.0% in nine months against 13.2%, which management attributes to efficiency initiatives [Management Language; CP-1A operating model]. Light capital intensity: USD 28.8 million of capital expenditure in nine months [Documentary Fact; CP-1]. No sponsor extraction: no related-party leakage or creditor-adverse action is documented, though the legal documents are not supplied [Insufficient Information on legal capacity; CP-1A governance].

Weaknesses. Customer and contract concentration: about 60% of revenue from ten contracts, about 55% from the federal government, and termination for convenience in almost all contracts [Documentary Fact; CP-1A]. Seasonal and delayed cash flow: operating cash flow was an outflow of USD 179.9 million in nine months and days sales outstanding were 98 days [Documentary Fact; CP-1]. Rising leverage funded by buybacks: net debt to issuer-adjusted EBITDA of 2.25x against 1.60x, with management comfortable at up to 3x on its covenant definition [Analyst Interpretation; CP-1, CP-1A]. Thin cash: USD 57.0 million of unrestricted cash against USD 96.3 million of restricted cash held for customers [Documentary Fact; CP-1]. Declining revenue: fiscal Q3 revenue down 5.1% and nine-month revenue down 4.4%, with Outside the U.S. guided to break even [Documentary Fact; CP-1, CP-1A]. Lowered outlook and customer modification through December 31, 2026 [Documentary Fact and Management Language; CP-1A]. Floating-rate exposure of USD 978.5 million with a USD 75.0 million swap expiring in September 2026 [Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1]. Intangible-heavy balance sheet: goodwill and intangibles USD 2,257.6 million against equity of USD 1,740.6 million [Documentary Fact; CP-1 C14]. Missing creditor protections: Credit Agreement restrictions, amendment terms, guarantors, ratings and ownership detail [Insufficient Information].
### Credit assessment
| Assessment | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Fundamental credit view: moderately levered, covenant-compliant government services operator with long contract visibility, rising leverage, seasonal cash flow and heavy contract concentration; the fourth-quarter collections and the capital allocation policy are the main watch items | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 financials, liquidity, debt register and covenant tables; CP-1A operating model and governance rows |

| Business risk: moderate, supported by backlog and essential government programs, offset by contract concentration, termination rights and a lowered outlook | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1A company and operating model |
| Financial risk: moderate on 2.25x net leverage and wide reported covenant headroom, with cash flow timing risk | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 financials table |
| Liquidity: adequate, USD 787.0 million, revolver-dependent | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 liquidity table |

| Creditor protection and ranking | Insufficient Information | Insufficient Information | Credit Agreement, amendment, guarantor and collateral detail beyond the 10-K sentence, ratings and the proxy statement are not supplied; this limits covenant, ranking and legal capacity conclusions |

Confidence is below High because the upstream readiness judgments for this module are READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS and the upstream gaps ledgers list High-severity gaps for the Credit Agreement, guarantors and the period after August 6, 2026.
### Thesis

MAXIMUS, INC. is an essential-services government contractor whose backlog, covenant headroom and long-dated bank facility support moderate leverage, provided fourth-quarter collections arrive, contract concentration does not produce a loss of a top contract, and shareholder returns do not outrun free cash flow.
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity | Basis |

| Collection timing on a large federal contract | Receivables rose to USD 1,382.0 million with days sales outstanding at 98; guidance depends on fourth-quarter collections | A slip in collections would leave the revolver as the only liquidity and push year-end leverage above management's range | Material | CP-1 C13, liquidity table; CP-1A operating model |

| Contract concentration and termination | About 60% of revenue from ten contracts and about one-fifth from one agency; almost all contracts terminable for convenience; a customer modification already lowers earnings | One decision changes earnings, covenant EBITDA and cash within a quarter | Material | CP-1A concentration and operating model rows |

| Debt-funded shareholder returns | Buybacks of USD 447.5 million in fiscal 2025 and USD 204.9 million in nine months 2026 funded by term loan expansions | Leverage can move toward the top of the 2x to 3x range before a contractual limit is evident | Material | CP-1A governance; CP-1 C11 |

| Covenant and definition uncertainty | The two covenants run on a Credit Agreement EBITDA that adds pro forma adjustments and stock compensation, and the agreement is not supplied | Reported headroom cannot be verified or rebuilt | Material | CP-1 C9; CP-0 gap |

| Floating-rate exposure | USD 978.5 million unhedged; Term Loan B swap of USD 75.0 million expires September 2026 | Interest cost rises with SOFR; modest relative to LTM issuer-adjusted EBITDA | Minor | CP-1 C12 |

| Declining revenue base | Fiscal Q3 revenue down 5.1%, Outside the U.S. at break even, lowered guidance | Falling volumes erode margin on a labor-based cost base | Material | CP-1 latest quarter; CP-1A |

| Contingent claims | MOVEit litigation accrual unquantified; indemnification of USD 8.8 million; performance bonds USD 33.2 million | Unquantified cash outflow risk, small relative to liquidity on known amounts | Minor | CP-1 claims table |

| Refinancing | USD 690.2 million due in fiscal 2029 and USD 778.9 million after; the amended Term Loan B maturity is not stated | Low near-term risk; refinancing terms unknown | Minor | CP-1 maturities chart |
### Debt, liquidity and covenant summary
| Item | Figure | Category | Basis |

| Debt principal, June 30, 2026 | USD 1,653.5 million (carrying value USD 1,636.9 million): Term Loan A USD 819.4 million, Term Loan B USD 814.2 million, revolver USD 20.0 million | Documentary Fact | CP-1 debt register |
| Cash and cash equivalents | USD 57.0 million unrestricted; USD 96.3 million restricted | Documentary Fact | CP-1 liquidity table |
| Revolver capacity not drawn | USD 730.0 million as printed (commitment USD 750 million, drawn USD 20.0 million); letters of credit not stated | Documentary Fact | CP-1 liquidity table |
| Liquidity | USD 787.0 million | Analyst Interpretation | CP-1 C10 |

| Maturities | USD 19.0 million July to September 2026; USD 75.8 million in fiscal 2027; USD 81.4 million in fiscal 2028; USD 690.2 million in fiscal 2029; USD 8.3 million in fiscal 2030; USD 778.9 million thereafter | Documentary Fact | CP-1 maturities chart |
| Hedging | USD 675.0 million of swaps, 40.8% of principal | Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation | CP-1 C12 |
| Reported covenant ratios | Net total leverage 2.00 (maximum 4.00); net interest coverage 8.72 (minimum 3.00) | Management Language (issuer-reported) | CP-1 covenant table |
| Analyst leverage | 2.33x gross and 2.25x net on LTM issuer-adjusted EBITDA | Analyst Interpretation | CP-1 C5 |
| Analyst interest cover | 8.24x EBITDA over cash interest paid | Analyst Interpretation | CP-1 C6 |
| Off-balance-sheet receivable sales | Facility of USD 350.0 million; USD 1.28 billion sold in nine months; balance outstanding not printed | Documentary Fact | CP-1 claims table |
### Latest quarter and after

Fiscal Q3 2026 revenue was USD 1,279.0 million, down 5.1%, with operating income of USD 161.4 million and issuer-adjusted EBITDA of USD 192.3 million, a 15.0% margin. On May 27, 2026 the Credit Agreement was amended and Term Loan B was increased by USD 325 million; the revolver fell from USD 225.0 million to USD 20.0 million, and debt principal rose USD 106.7 million in the quarter. In nine months the issuer repurchased about 2.6 million shares at a cost of USD 192.4 million. After June 30, 2026 it collected USD 245 million from the delayed federal customer, declared a quarterly dividend of USD 0.33 per share on July 6, 2026 and began a customer-directed contract modification that runs through December 31, 2026. In August 2026 it lowered its earnings and free cash flow outlook [CP-1 latest quarter; CP-1A timeline]. Nothing dated after August 6, 2026 is supplied, including fiscal Q4 results.
## Calculations
Inputs are the upstream handoff figures cited. Results are rounded as shown.

- **C1, interest sensitivity (inference).** Unhedged principal 419,375 + 539,173 + 20,000 = 978,548 thousand (CP-1 C12); a 100 basis point rise adds 978,548 x 1% = 9,785 thousand, USD 9.8 million a year, which is 11.3% of LTM cash interest paid of 86,279 thousand (9,785 / 86,279). It assumes a full year at the June 30, 2026 balances and ignores the September 2026 swap expiry.

- **C2, liquidity cover of near-term principal.** Liquidity 786,953 thousand (CP-1 C10) / principal due July 2026 to September 2027, 18,952 + 75,809 = 94,761 thousand = 8.3x. Through fiscal 2028: 94,761 + 81,434 = 176,195 thousand, 4.5x.

- **C3, room to the top of management's range (Credit Agreement basis, illustrative).** At 3.00x on Credit Agreement EBITDA of 798,419 thousand, net debt would be 2,395,257 thousand against 1,596,595 thousand today, an increase of 798,662 thousand. At the 4.00 covenant maximum the increase is 1,597,081 thousand (CP-1 C9). This ignores EBITDA change and is not a forecast or a capacity statement.

- **C4, shareholder returns against cash generation.** LTM dividends 68,282 + LTM share purchases 345,958 = 414,240 thousand, 95.6% of LTM free cash flow of 433,230 thousand (CP-1 C1, C3). Nine months: returns 256,356 thousand against free cash flow of −208,615 thousand, a gap of 464,971 thousand; net borrowing of 302,740 and a fall in unrestricted cash of 222,351 − 56,953 = 165,398 together are 468,138 thousand, and other cash flows are not itemised here.
- **C5, capitalization.** Debt principal 1,653,548 / (1,653,548 + equity 1,740,551) = 48.7%. Goodwill plus intangibles of 2,257,574 exceed equity by 517,023 (CP-1 C14).

- **C6, leverage including operating leases (illustrative).** Principal 1,653,548 + operating lease liabilities 94,883 = 1,748,431 thousand; / LTM issuer-adjusted EBITDA 711,009 = 2.46x. Net of unrestricted cash: (1,748,431 − 56,953) = 1,691,478 / 711,009 = 2.38x. Lease expense is inside EBITDA, so this overstates leverage and is shown only as a sensitivity.

- **C7, collections already received against guidance.** Implied fourth-quarter free cash flow 633,615 to 683,615 thousand (CP-1 C13); the 245,000 thousand collected after June 30, 2026 is 38.7% to 35.8% of it (245,000 / 633,615 and 245,000 / 683,615). The 245,000 is operating cash received and not net of fourth-quarter outflows.

- **C8, upstream figures reused.** Leverage, cover, covenant headroom, liquidity, maturities, hedge share, backlog ratios and revenue shares are taken from CP-1 (C1 to C16) and CP-1A (C1 to C8) and are not recomputed.
## Gaps
| Gap | Why it matters | Severity | Action |

| Credit Agreement text, the May 27, 2026 amendment terms and the Consolidated EBITDA definition are not supplied | Headroom, legal capacity for distributions, baskets and the amended Term Loan B maturity cannot be verified | High | Supply the executed agreement and amendment |

| Guarantor entities, collateral beyond the 10-K sentence and the restricted or unrestricted split are not supplied | Ranking and structural position of the bank debt cannot be assessed | High | Supply the guarantor schedule |

| Fiscal Q4 and fiscal 2026 results and all events from August 7, 2026 to the cutoff are not supplied | Guidance depends on fourth-quarter collections; new financing or ratings could change the view | High | Supply the fiscal 2026 10-K and any 8-K, or confirm none |

| Contract-level detail and the identity of the customer behind the modification are not supplied | Concentration and renewal risk behind the ten largest contracts cannot be sized | High | Supply contract and recompete schedules |
| Ratings and market prices are not supplied | No external credit opinion to compare against | Medium | Supply rating reports or keep Not supplied |
| Proxy statement (ownership percentages, board, related parties) not supplied | Governance and control rights cannot be assessed | Medium | Supply the 2026 proxy statement |

| Letters of credit under the revolver at June 30, 2026, Canada and United Kingdom facility terms, and receivable-sale balances not printed | Liquidity may be overstated by unreported usage | Medium | Request later disclosure |

| Customer modification effect on full-year earnings has no bridge between the 10-Q per-quarter figure and the revised guidance ranges | The size of the earnings effect through fiscal 2027 is unquantified | Medium | Treat as separate attributed figures |
| MOVEit litigation accrual and insurance recovery not printed | Contingent cash outflow cannot be sized | Medium | Carry as an unquantified contingency |

| Three logged source conflicts (fiscal 2025 buyback amount, federal revenue share definition, Outside the U.S. margin outlook) | Capital returned and concentration must be quoted with their definitions | Low | Quote the figure with its basis |

The illustrative calculations C1, C3, C6 and C7 are analyst constructions and should be labelled so.
